How this is made
  • Movie (toy spirals): two MLPs with 10 layers of width 16 and ReLU were trained on 400 fixed two-spirals points (the data of the Going deep playground) with full-batch gradient descent (all 400 points at every step, learning rate 0.05, 6,000 steps), so the loss function is exactly the same at every step. One is plain, the other residual (a skip connection around each hidden layer). At 95 moments (dense early) we drew the loss on a 81 x 81 slice around the current weights over a, b in [-1, 1], along two random directions drawn once and kept for the whole movie, rescaled to the current weights each time (every row of each weight matrix gets the norm of the same row of the current weights; biases get zero). The vertical axis is the loss itself (linear, heights above loss 3 cut flat), with one fixed scale for every frame and both networks. Between the 95 stored frames the heights are blended for a smooth animation. Computed offline in PyTorch; nothing is trained in the page. One seed per network.
  • Movies 2 to 5 (two moons, XOR): same method as the spirals movie (81 x 81 slice, filter-normalised random directions drawn once, heights are the loss, linear, with one fixed scale per movie (cut flat above loss 3 for the first), 86 frames dense early). Convex vs non-convex: 200 moons points (noise 0.2), full-batch gradient descent for 1,500 steps; logistic regression (learning rate 0.02) against a 6-layer, width-16 ReLU MLP (learning rate 0.05); slice range 1.5. Basin radius is measured along 24 random directions as the distance at which the loss has risen by 0.3 above its value at the network; one seed. Small vs large learning rate (movie 4): 200 moons points (noise 0.4), a tanh MLP with 4 layers of width 4 (62 weights), full-batch gradient descent for 30,000 steps with learning rate 0.15 against 0.5 from the same start; the slice axes are the top two eigenvectors of the exact Hessian at the current weights, range 0.5 in weight units, cut flat above loss 1.5; sharpness is the top Hessian eigenvalue. One seed (other seeds gave 11.9 against 8.3 and 19.8 against 5.4, and some did not settle cleanly). XOR (movie 5): the 4 XOR points, a tanh 2-2-2 network, learning rate 0.3, 1,500 steps; the slice plane goes through the current weights, the copy with the two hidden units swapped and the copy with hidden unit 0 sign-flipped (all the same function), range from -0.5 to 1.5 along both axes, cut flat above loss 3; a second start looked almost identical. A small-batch against large-batch “flat vs sharp” pair was also tried and dropped: the small-batch run ended sharper but also at a lower loss, so the comparison was not fair.
  • FashionMNIST views below. Two MLPs of width 128 were trained on FashionMNIST while the weights were saved along the way: a plain stack of ReLU + BatchNorm layers, and a residual one (skip connections, BatchNorm). Depth 32 trained for 5 epochs (2,345 SGD steps, learning rate 0.03), depth 56 for 240 epochs (112,560 steps, learning rate 0.01; a 15-epoch run left the plain net at 45% test accuracy and a 60-epoch run at 47.5% while it was still improving, so both nets were retrained longer); momentum 0.9, batch 128, one seed.
  • The loss is always measured on the same 2000 training images, with BatchNorm using the statistics of those images (so the loss depends only on the weights). Test accuracy is on the FashionMNIST test set at that checkpoint. Everything was computed offline in PyTorch; this page only draws the stored numbers, nothing is trained live.
  • Path on a fixed plane (Li et al. 2018, arXiv 1712.09913, section 7): the weights were saved every 50 steps plus extra early ones. The two main directions (PCA) of "weights at step t minus final weights" define a plane through the final weights. The surface is the loss on that plane (41 x 41 grid). The path is each saved network projected onto the plane; it is drawn on the surface at the projected point; the loss quoted in the numbers is that network’s true loss (all its weights), which can differ from the surface there because the plane holds only part of the movement. The first jump away from the random start can be far longer than the rest, so the frame is sized for the later path and the earliest points are pinned to its edge.
  • Landscape around the network: at 15 checkpoints, a 31 x 31 slice of the loss around the current weights, over a, b in [-1, 1], along two random directions. They are filter-normalized (every row of each weight matrix is rescaled to the norm of the same row in the current weights; biases and BatchNorm parameters get zero), so a distance of 1 means a change as large as the weights themselves. The directions are the same random draw at every checkpoint, rescaled to the current weights. Between checkpoints the heights are blended, which is only for a smooth animation.
  • Limits: one run and one seed per network. The plain depth-32 and depth-56 nets end at worse solutions than the residual ones (74% and 55.6% test accuracy against 88% and 89%), and the plain depth-56 net is still improving after 240 epochs (training loss on the 2000 images 0.69, against 0.0017 for the residual net), so part of the difference in the pictures is solution quality, not only architecture.
